facts.text: My right leg has gone numb.

facts.item: numbness in the right leg: onset
facts.text: It came on suddenly, about three months after I started my HIV medicines.

facts.item: numbness in the right leg: course
facts.text: It has spread over about a month.

facts.item: numbness in the right leg: location
facts.text: Now my whole right leg and the right side of my belly are numb.
I haven't had any other whole-body symptoms.
I've had weakness on my left side since I first fell ill a few months ago.
When I first fell ill a few months ago, I had a headache.
I have HIV; it was diagnosed when I first fell ill, about four months before this numbness began.
At the same time I was diagnosed with toxoplasmosis with lesions in my brain.
With the toxoplasmosis treatment my symptoms got better, and I was told the brain scans improved too.
I've stayed on my toxoplasmosis medicine; it was later switched to a lower, suppressive dose.
I wasn't given any steroids with the toxoplasmosis treatment.
I started HIV medicines one month after I was diagnosed, so about three months before the numbness began.
I also take preventive medicine against MAC (Mycobacterium avium complex).
I take all my treatments exactly as prescribed; I haven't missed any.

findings.result: Prior left hemiparesis; strength preserved in the affected right-sided areas.

findings.name: sensory examination
findings.result: Sensory level at T9 on the right, with loss of touch and pain sensation below this level; proprioception preserved in the affected areas.

findings.name: follow-up brain CT
findings.result: Some prior lesions improved, others slightly worsened with ring enhancement and edema, and several new lesions appeared.

aliases: central nervous system immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome
gold.reasoning: 1. Progression of toxoplasmosis infection — “The differential diagnosis between IRIS and a progression of toxoplasmosis infection is difficult, but if the last hypothesis was true, most probably a marked worsening of all the previous lesions would be present in the brain CT scan.” 2. Central nervous system lymphoma — “a normal CSF lymphocyte phenotype assay and a whole-body positron emission tomography (PET) scan revealed neither hyper-metabolic cerebral nor medullar lesions, which ruled out CNS lymphoma.” 3. HTLV-I/II infection — “Serological HTLV-I/II antibody assay was negative.” 4. Paradoxical immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome — “The clinical and laboratory information suggested a potential case of CNS-IRIS.”

The HAART regimen is not given ('as per institutional protocol').
notes: Index visit: the later visit for right-leg numbness, about four months after starting HAART (s006–s012, s014–s015). The case opens with the initial presentation (s001–s005: headache, left hemiparesis, new HIV with cerebral toxoplasmosis), but the gold diagnosis can only be made at the later visit (selection note: the treatment timeline is the key clue), so that visit is the index and s001–s005 are history (patient facts) and earlier findings with a time.

Treatment before the index visit (anti-toxoplasma therapy without steroids, HAART, MAC prophylaxis) is medication history; its earlier response (f011) is part of the patient's history, not a workup outcome.
Psychomotor retardation at the initial presentation is an observer sign; it is kept only in the earlier examination finding (x019).
f006 is a blanket denial of systemic symptoms; it answers only a general question, not a specific symptom such as weight loss or night sweats.
s013: CSF PCR for Toxoplasma gondii was not performed, so there is no finding; a request for it is answered as unavailable.
